newsitem.title: CHINA: Top China mobile-phone maker posts solid results.
newsitem.headline: Top China mobile-phone maker posts solid results.

text.p: China's largest cellular phone maker, Eastern Communications Co, posted solid 1996 results on Thursday but the firm's shares fell on investor disappointment with its dividend plans, brokers said.
The company's annual report said net profit for 1996 rose by 14.29 percent to 291.618 million yuan from 255.162 million yuan for 1995 based on international accounting standards.
Based on domestic accounting standards, the 1996 profit was 322.182 million yuan against 262.474 million yuan in 1995.
"The overall profit situation is very good, it is 103 percent over our original target," said a company spokesman.
But the firm's foreign currency B shares, listed in Shanghai, ended the day at US$0.946, down $0.068 or 6.75 percent while its domestic A shares closed at its 10 percent limit-down or 24.38 yuan.

The company's board of directors proposed a cash dividend of 0.175 yuan per share for B share holders and 0.048 yuan per share for A share holders from profits in 1996, pending the approval of a shareholders' meeting.
Brokers said the dividend payments were lower than investors had expected.

"The results are satisfactory," said a broker with a major Chinese brokerage. "Competition in the portable phone market was very fierce in 1996 but the company was helped by its good management and marketing strategy."
A stock analyst in Hong Kong who watches the company said its profits were slightly below expectations, but still acceptable.

"I would expect a further 10 percent growth in profits for 1997, but I don't see any meaningful contribution in the short-term from the two cellular phone joint ventures with U.S.-based Motorola," the analyst said.

Using Motorola technology, Eastern produces all three types of cellular phone systems available in China -- analog, Global System for Mobile (GSM) Communications, and code division multiple access (CDMA). Its two Motorola joint ventures are due to go into production this year.
The company said in a statement that the results were helped by a strong domestic market for cellular telephones.
"Facing fierce competition, the firm set up more sales and maintenance outlets around China in 1996 and managed to ensure good production and results," it said.
"Competition will even be more fierce in 1997," said one broker. "But the company is expected to weather the storm and maintain steady growth partly due to China's bulging portable phone market."

China is now the fourth-largest mobile phone market in the world after the United States, Japan and Britain. With only about four out of every 1,000 people using them, China has huge market potential, analysts said.
But Eastern Communications faces competition from both foreign portable phone makers which are targeting China, and from another Motorola operation in Tianjin, analysts said.
"The market share for the Motorola Tianjin joint venture is growing very fast and poses a threat to Eastern Communications," said one broker.
Analysts said Eastern Communications' excellent relations with China's Ministry of Post and Telecommunications would help it to keep winning business.
